citation: Konstantopoulos, S., Miller, S. R., & van der Ploeg, A. (2013). The impact of Indiana's system of interim assessments on mathematics and reading achievement. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, 35(4), 481-499. https://doi.org/10.3102/0162373713498930
report_number: EEPA 35(4):481-499 (published article paywalled). Numbers extracted from the legal open-access working-paper version: Konstantopoulos, S., Miller, S., van der Ploeg, A., Li, C.-H., & Traynor, A. The Impact of Indiana's System of Benchmark Assessments on Mathematics Achievement (SREE Fall 2011 conference paper; AIR institutional repository).
design: School-level two-level cluster RCT (students nested in schools). Indiana statewide interim/diagnostic assessment system (mCLASS:Math in K-2; CTB/McGraw-Hill Acuity in grades 3-8) + teacher training/PD on using the diagnostic data, vs business-as-usual control schools (no assessment program). 59 schools randomized (35 treatment, 24 control) in 2009-2010; 49 participated the whole year (31 treatment, 18 control); ~20,000 students K-8. Outcome = ISTEP+ Indiana state achievement test (mathematics in this OA working paper). Impacts via two-level HLM with grade fixed effects; outcome z-standardized within grade so estimates are standardized mean differences (SD units). Subject = mathematics (STEM); registry grade band 3-6 (Acuity grades).
problems: ASSIGNED STUDY = Konstantopoulos, Miller & van der Ploeg (2013), EEPA 35(4):481-499, DOI 10.3102/0162373713498930. The PUBLISHED article (which covers BOTH mathematics AND reading) is PAYWALLED: OpenAlex is_oa=false/oa_status=closed and Unpaywall returns no OA location; no legal OA copy of the published version was found (AERA is not OA). I therefore extracted from the LEGAL open-access working-paper version of the SAME experiment, hosted on the AIR institutional repository (Konstantopoulos, Miller, van der Ploeg, Li & Traynor, SREE Fall 2011 conference paper, 'The Impact of Indiana's System of Benchmark Assessments on Mathematics Achievement'). This working paper is MATHEMATICS-ONLY: it reports the identical 59-school 2009-2010 Indiana interim-assessment RCT (same authors, same mCLASS+Acuity intervention, same ISTEP+ outcome) but presents only the math results. Consequence: (1) NO reading effect sizes could be extracted because the reading analysis appears only in the paywalled published article. (2) Math estimates in the working paper may differ slightly from the final published EEPA figures. The estimates are model-based mean differences already in within-grade SD units (z-scored outcome), so impact_estimate = d directly; Hedges J small-sample correction is ~1.000 at these large df, so g ~= d. Cluster_adjusted=true (two-level HLM SEs). ICC not reported as a single design-effect value (multilevel model used) so icc=null per spec (never guess). n_t/n_c per cell not separately reported (only total N per cell and overall school counts 35T/24C assigned, 31T/18C participating), so per-cell n_t/n_c left null. Extracted ITT (Intention-to-Treat) Model II (covariate-adjusted) estimates as the primary, unbiased experimental contrasts; TOT estimates are larger (noted). The 'TPD for digital tools' descriptor refers to teacher PD/training on using the mCLASS/Acuity digital diagnostic-assessment tools. Registry grade band is 3-6, so the four within-grade STEM contrasts (grades 3,4,5,6) precisely cover the band; the grades 3-8 aggregate is also extracted as a composite (it additionally includes sparse grades 7-8).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Interim/diagnostic assessment system (Acuity, grades 3-8) + teacher PD on using the digital diagnostic data, vs business-as-usual control; grades 3-8 aggregate
effect_sizes.test_name: ISTEP+ (Indiana Statewide Testing for Educational Progress-Plus) mathematics; z-standardized within grade
effect_sizes.g_method: Model-based standardized treatment effect (d = 0.186) taken directly from the two-level HLM (outcome z-scored within grade -> estimate is already a standardized mean difference). Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = N-2 = 11850 gives J=0.99994, so g = J*d = 0.18599. g_se = J*impact_se = 0.077; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.005928. SE is the HLM model SE (clustering accounted for).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.27, Table 3 (ITT, Grades 3 to 8, Model II: Estimate 0.186*, SE 0.077, N schools=56, N students=11852)
effect_sizes.notes: ITT, Model II (adds student & school characteristics: age, race, gender, SES, special-ed, LEP, school-level composition; grade fixed effects). p<=.05 (starred). Aggregate over grades 3-8; grades 7-8 are sparse (sensitivity analysis omitting 7-8 gave very similar estimates), so this is a good proxy for the registry's 3-6 STEM band. N students = 11,852 (Model II); N schools = 56. Model I (treatment only) for the same cell: est 0.141, SE 0.088 (ns). TOT Model II grades 3-8: est 0.257*, SE 0.076 (Table 4). For grades 4-6 the authors also ran models adding prior achievement (pretest) and reported results 'similar to those reported here', but those pretest-adjusted figures are not separately tabled, so pretest_adjusted set false for the tabled Model II. Marked composite because it subsumes the grade 3,4,5,6 subscale rows below (and additionally grades 7-8).
